correctness.rationale: Quartic character orthogonality gives an exact 64-term expression for each triple count N_p(e), with the unique all-zero character contribution p−3, nine one-nonzero terms bounded by 2, 27 two-nonzero terms bounded by sqrt(p)+1 and 27 three-nonzero terms bounded by 2sqrt(p). Thus 64N≥p−81sqrt(p)−48>0 for all eligible p≥6724. In the remaining finite interval, source standard-library sieve, primitive-root enumeration and independent quartic-power classification exhaust **all 427** primes p≡1 (mod4); independent full enumeration recovered exactly 38 exceptional primes, last at p=1153 with sole missing word (0,0,0), and last missing other word p=709. Accordingly all 64 words occur for p≥1181, with sharp predecessor p=1153; all nonzero words occur for p≥733, with sharp predecessor p=709. Bounded enumeration plus proven analytic cutoff together form the proof.
